title: chore: designate the six CQ epics' integration-and-hardening tasks with update_epic finalTaskId
description:
Board data only; no code changes. task-cd2e447728224044abe7fa669d42f7fb adds Epic.finalTaskId and makes get_context isEpicFinal follow it. No structural rule can pick CQ-F12 on its own, because bc8410af depends on F12 and was created after it, so the six CQ epics need an explicit designation.

This project's live daemon runs the IDE-bundled build. That build rejects finalTaskId until the plugin is rebuilt from a commit that contains task-cd2e447728224044abe7fa669d42f7fb and the daemon restarts. Promote this row only after that. Probe with one moe.update_epic call first: an "is not a supported epic update field" error means the daemon is still on the old build.

Designate:
- CQ-F epic-5d9f6c0a3b0a4a6882d2a74387a3f56d -> task-72184c6505cc41e8b6066732011ffb70 [CQ-F12]
- CQ-R epic-fe5e32c32b044a20944c693dfd79411b -> task-f4811a729f9e436ba129a65c12d348c1 [CQ-R13]
- CQ-V epic-f5c1c2ea674e40bcad8ab16d7657ccc0 -> task-b621ddc99fe44d50ab700b2aa51c84fc [CQ-V12]
- CQ-C epic-9d76d843b4ec484987139b930d1d681e -> task-4e0264fc52e04574a9d10ef602281ca3 [CQ-C11]
- CQ-I epic-c9561bfb767248e38c9c0be82d09ec2c -> task-4e412148225f480c8c0d5a1706a3cc76 [CQ-I06]
- CQ-M epic-b8c6bbda4def46cbb8d1b351f8ea3eeb -> task-ced857485a1c4d75b57cc25dcc9b4d82 [CQ-M06]

Go through moe.update_epic only. Never edit .moe/epics/*.json by hand.
definitionOfDone: moe.update_epic { epicId, finalTaskId } has been called through the daemon for each of the six CQ epics, with the hardening task listed in the description, and no .moe/ file was edited by hand.

moe.get_context reports isEpicFinal true for F12, R13, V12, C11, I06 and M06, and false for each epic's highest-order non-ARCHIVED sibling at the time of the check. The six F12/R13/V12/C11/I06/M06 get_context outputs and the sibling checks are supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Human-gated: promote only after the daemon serving this project runs a build that contains task-cd2e447728224044abe7fa669d42f7fb (moe.update_epic accepts finalTaskId).

implementationPlan.description:
Probe the live daemon, then designate CQ-F. This changes board data only: no code, no repo files, no new tests. The regression tests for the designation rule landed with task-cd2e4477 (updateEpic.test.ts, getContext.test.ts, and its frozen six-epic fixture). Use moe.update_epic only. Never edit .moe/epics/*.json or any other .moe file by hand.

1. Gate check, read-only:
- The dependsOn gate already holds this row until task-cd2e4477 is DONE.
- The live daemon must also run a build that contains it (landing 4137865).
- Look at your moe update_epic tool's input schema. As of 2026-10-27 09:15Z the live schema had NO finalTaskId property: the IDE-bundled build was still old.
- If the property is missing, or the first call below fails with 'is not a supported epic update field', or a client-side schema validation refuses the key, nothing has been written.
- In that case call moe.report_blocked with reason: 'live daemon lacks update_epic finalTaskId: a human must rebuild the JetBrains plugin from a commit containing 4137865 (task-cd2e4477) and restart the daemon'. Pass no blockedOnTaskIds, because the blocker is a human action, not a task. Then end the session. Do not retry in a loop, and do not route around it with a hand edit.
- scripts/moe-call.sh update_epic '<json>' is an acceptable route to the same moe.update_epic tool when only the CLI-side schema is stale. It is never a way past an old daemon.

2. Record the CQ-F epic's current title, description, epicRails, status and order, using moe.get_context on task-72184c6505cc41e8b6066732011ffb70 (its epic block) or the update response. You will use these for the step-4 drift check.

3. Call moe.update_epic { epicId: 'epic-5d9f6c0a3b0a4a6882d2a74387a3f56d', finalTaskId: 'task-72184c6505cc41e8b6066732011ffb70' } ([CQ-F12]).

4. Error handling:
- Success requires the response's epic.finalTaskId to equal the id.
- An 'Invalid finalTaskId: …' refusal (no such task, another epic, or ARCHIVED) means the board moved since planning. Stop and report_blocked naming the refusal. Never substitute a different task without a human.

Designate the other five epics, one moe.update_epic call each. Read every response:
- CQ-R epic-fe5e32c32b044a20944c693dfd79411b -> task-f4811a729f9e436ba129a65c12d348c1 [CQ-R13]
- CQ-V epic-f5c1c2ea674e40bcad8ab16d7657ccc0 -> task-b621ddc99fe44d50ab700b2aa51c84fc [CQ-V12]
- CQ-C epic-9d76d843b4ec484987139b930d1d681e -> task-4e0264fc52e04574a9d10ef602281ca3 [CQ-C11]
- CQ-I epic-c9561bfb767248e38c9c0be82d09ec2c -> task-4e412148225f480c8c0d5a1706a3cc76 [CQ-I06]
- CQ-M epic-b8c6bbda4def46cbb8d1b351f8ea3eeb -> task-ced857485a1c4d75b57cc25dcc9b4d82 [CQ-M06]

At planning time (2026-10-27) every target existed in its own epic and none was ARCHIVED: R13, V12 and C11 were BACKLOG, I06 and M06 BLOCKED, F12 REVIEW.

Send only epicId and finalTaskId, never any other field. The call is idempotent, so repeating it with the same id is harmless. The error handling is the same as in step 1: an 'Invalid finalTaskId' refusal or a transport error stops the step, and you report what you saw (report_blocked if it cannot be resolved without a human). A partial run is acceptable to resume; it is not acceptable to paper over.

Verification, run once.

1. For each epic, find its highest-order non-ARCHIVED sibling at check time: moe.list_tasks { epicId } (ARCHIVED rows are hidden by default); take the highest `order` other than the designated task, and every row at that order if there are ties. The expected siblings as of 2026-10-27:
- F: task-bc8410afe7144ddda804b60af000864d (249.5)
- R: task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (249.5)
- V: task-6a5d5a13257b48c9940ae3b22347ff7d (244.5)
- C: task-d75f71d7664848fd859a3f877e74ba43 (241.5)
- I: task-758bb59a61bd443382e02aea44b515c9 (I06 itself is the highest, so its next sibling, 246.5)
- M: task-c53999b2dd2c4ad08bacb73c50371cfa (229.5)
If any has changed, substitute the current id in the command below.

2. Run this exact command from the repository root, in your own shell so the wrapper's MOE_PROJECT_PATH applies. It must exit 0, and its 12 lines are the outputTail for moe.complete_task:
( fail=0; for pair in task-72184c6505cc41e8b6066732011ffb70:true task-bc8410afe7144ddda804b60af000864d:false task-f4811a729f9e436ba129a65c12d348c1:true task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e:false task-b621ddc99fe44d50ab700b2aa51c84fc:true task-6a5d5a13257b48c9940ae3b22347ff7d:false task-4e0264fc52e04574a9d10ef602281ca3:true task-d75f71d7664848fd859a3f877e74ba43:false task-4e412148225f480c8c0d5a1706a3cc76:true task-758bb59a61bd443382e02aea44b515c9:false task-ced857485a1c4d75b57cc25dcc9b4d82:true task-c53999b2dd2c4ad08bacb73c50371cfa:false; do id=${pair%%:*}; want=${pair##*:}; got=$(bash scripts/moe-call.sh get_context "{\"taskId\":\"$id\"}" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{let v="ERR";try{v=String(JSON.parse(s).task.isEpicFinal)}catch(e){}process.stdout.write(v)})'); echo "$id isEpicFinal=$got want=$want"; [ "$got" = "$want" ] || fail=1; done; exit $fail )

Error handling: an unreachable daemon, an error reply, or a missing isEpicFinal prints ERR, which fails the run. Never reformat ERR into a pass.

3. Also make the same 12 checks with your own moe.get_context tool. Paste a compact table (task id, epic, isEpicFinal, expected) into the complete_task summary, since the DoD requires those outputs.

Both reads are expected side effects:
- each default get_context stamps your id into that task's contextFetchedBy, which is benign bookkeeping;
- no served-context receipt is minted, because you own none of those attempts;
- view:'status' cannot be used, because it omits isEpicFinal.

Self-review, run once. Check before moe.complete_task:
- Each of the six update responses shows only finalTaskId changed. Title, description, architectureNotes, epicRails, status and order must equal the values recorded beforehand. Diff the CQ-F epic block from step 1; for the other five, compare the update response with a get_context epic block read before the call.
- `git status --short -- .moe/epics` shows only the six daemon-written epic records changing, and you edited no .moe file yourself. The landing stages them as BOARD paths when settings.commitBoardState is on. Leave any other .moe or repo path you see alone, because peers own it.
- No other epic was touched, and no task status, priority or dependency changed.
- The verification table holds 6 true and 6 false, and the command exited 0.
If something is wrong, fix it with another moe.update_epic call (finalTaskId '' clears a designation), then rerun the step-3 command and submit only fresh exit-0 evidence. This task adds no code test because it changes data only. Say that in the summary and point to task-cd2e4477's tests as the logic coverage.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Choices made, with the rejected alternatives:
1. Blocking now instead of planning was rejected. The plan is fully determined, and the WORKING claim is already gated by dependsOn task-cd2e4477, which is still in REVIEW. The remaining environmental gate, the plugin rebuild plus daemon restart, is checked at execution by a no-write probe. If that probe fails, it parks the row with report_blocked.
2. A hand edit of .moe/epics was rejected: it is forbidden.
3. Verifying with view:'status' was rejected, because it lacks isEpicFinal.
4. A new verification script file was rejected, because the task is data-only. An inline bash loop over scripts/moe-call.sh is re-runnable by QA instead. Its per-id body was dry-run from a WSL seat on this task itself: isEpicFinal=false, exit 0.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Checked during planning:
- At 2026-10-27 ~09:15Z the live tools/list schema for moe.update_epic had no finalTaskId (title, description, architectureNotes, epicRails, status, order only). The IDE-bundled daemon predates landing 4137865.
- update_epic validates finalTaskId before any write: the id must name a task, of the same epic, that is not ARCHIVED; "" clears the designation.
- isEpicFinalTask (delivery/policy.ts): a valid designation makes only that task final; otherwise the fallback is the highest order among non-ARCHIVED tasks, ties counting.
- get_context default reads stamp contextFetchedBy. Receipts are minted only for the owner of the running attempt.
- moe-call.sh prints the tool result JSON pretty-printed, and an error reply exits 1.
- Read-only board snapshot: F12 is REVIEW at order 234.5 under bc8410af (249.5); R13 is BACKLOG at 130 under 4f1e37f3 (249.5); V12 is BACKLOG at 120 under V06 (244.5); C11 is BACKLOG at 110 under C06 (241.5); I06 is BLOCKED and already highest at 247.5; M06 is BLOCKED and already highest at 230.5.
planningNotes.risks:
Risks for the worker to watch:
- If the daemon is still the old build, the probe parks the row. That is expected, not a failure.
- A CLI session started before a daemon upgrade may keep a stale tool schema. Use moe-call.sh, or relaunch, rather than assuming the daemon is old.
- Highest-order siblings can change, because new bug rows get high orders. Recompute them at check time.
- Do not ask governors to promote dependents. This row only designates.
- The epic records are board state. Peers' sessions may also land .moe/epics changes, so never stage or revert by hand.
